blocks.text: Śiva Sūtras 3.4
blocks.directed: [long pause] Śiva Sūtras 3.4

blocks.text: शरीरे संहारः कलानाम्
blocks.directed: [slowly] शरीरे संहारः कलानाम्

blocks.text: Śarīre saṃhāraḥ kalānām.
blocks.directed: Śarīre saṃhāraḥ kalānām.

blocks.text: In the body, the dissolution of the constituent powers or parts.
blocks.directed: In the body, the dissolution of the constituent powers or parts.

blocks.text: Right, Time to Uninstall the Universe from Your Body.
blocks.directed: Right, Time to Uninstall the Universe from Your Body.

blocks.text: We’ve arrived at our first major concrete contemplative instruction.
blocks.directed: We’ve arrived at our first major concrete contemplative instruction.

blocks.text: And Kṣemarāja explains it using bhāvanā.
blocks.directed: And Kṣemarāja explains it using bhāvanā.

blocks.text: Creative contemplation.
blocks.directed: Creative contemplation.

blocks.text: Or more precisely, an intentionally cultivated contemplative apprehension.
blocks.directed: Or more precisely, an intentionally cultivated contemplative apprehension.

blocks.text: Now, unlike the sudden recognition characteristic of Śāmbhavopāya, we’re working with structured practices.
blocks.directed: Now, unlike the sudden recognition characteristic of Śāmbhavopāya, we’re working with structured practices.

blocks.text: The practitioner deliberately employs the mind to transform the way manifestation is understood.
blocks.directed: The practitioner deliberately employs the mind to transform the way manifestation is understood.

blocks.text: And the practice here concerns the dissolution of the principles of manifestation into their sources.
blocks.directed: And the practice here concerns the dissolution of the principles of manifestation into their sources.

blocks.text: Saṃhāra.
blocks.directed: [slowly] Saṃhāra.

blocks.text: Withdrawal.
blocks.directed: Withdrawal.

blocks.text: Reabsorption.
blocks.directed: Reabsorption.

blocks.text: Dissolution.
blocks.directed: Dissolution.

blocks.text: Remember the thirty-six tattvas?
blocks.directed: Remember the thirty-six tattvas?

blocks.text: The entire hierarchy extending from Śiva down to earth?
blocks.directed: The entire hierarchy extending from Śiva down to earth?

blocks.text: Well, now we’re moving in reverse.
blocks.directed: Well, now we’re moving in reverse.

blocks.text: The universe has manifested through successive degrees of differentiation.
blocks.directed: The universe has manifested through successive degrees of differentiation.

blocks.text: The contemplative process reverses that movement.
blocks.directed: The contemplative process reverses that movement.

blocks.text: And the body becomes the field of practice.
blocks.directed: And the body becomes the field of practice.

blocks.text: Now, Kṣemarāja distinguishes three levels of embodiment.
blocks.directed: Now, Kṣemarāja distinguishes three levels of embodiment.

blocks.text: The gross body, constituted by the gross elements.
blocks.directed: The gross body, constituted by the gross elements.

blocks.text: The subtle body, including the mental faculties and subtle elements.
blocks.directed: The subtle body, including the mental faculties and subtle elements.

blocks.text: And a higher causal level, involving subtler conditions of consciousness and vital power extending towards Samanā.
blocks.directed: And a higher causal level, involving subtler conditions of consciousness and vital power extending towards Samanā.

blocks.text: The practitioner contemplates the progressive dissolution of the manifest principles.
blocks.directed: The practitioner contemplates the progressive dissolution of the manifest principles.

blocks.text: Earth is reabsorbed into its causal principle.
blocks.directed: Earth is reabsorbed into its causal principle.

blocks.text: And so on through the hierarchy.
blocks.directed: And so on through the hierarchy.

blocks.text: The differentiated structures of manifestation are traced back towards their ultimate source.
blocks.directed: The differentiated structures of manifestation are traced back towards their ultimate source.

blocks.text: But the point isn’t merely to memorise the thirty-six tattvas backwards like an exceptionally committed Sanskrit student.
blocks.directed: But the point isn’t merely to memorise the thirty-six tattvas backwards like an exceptionally committed Sanskrit student.

blocks.text: Although, to be fair, that would be quite impressive.
blocks.directed: Although, to be fair, that would be quite impressive.

blocks.text: The point is the transformation of how the practitioner understands the relationship between the manifest and its source.
blocks.directed: The point is the transformation of how the practitioner understands the relationship between the manifest and its source.

blocks.text: Imagine looking at a golden ornament.
blocks.directed: Imagine looking at a golden ornament.

blocks.text: A bracelet.
blocks.directed: A bracelet.

blocks.text: You can identify its particular form.
blocks.directed: You can identify its particular form.

blocks.text: Its weight.
blocks.directed: Its weight.

blocks.text: Its decoration.
blocks.directed: Its decoration.

blocks.text: Its shape.
blocks.directed: Its shape.

blocks.text: But you can also recognise that the bracelet’s existence depends upon the gold.
blocks.directed: But you can also recognise that the bracelet’s existence depends upon the gold.

blocks.text: The bracelet is not an independent substance standing apart from the gold.
blocks.directed: The bracelet is not an independent substance standing apart from the gold.

blocks.text: Now imagine reversing the process conceptually.
blocks.directed: Now imagine reversing the process conceptually.

blocks.text: You cease attending to the bracelet as a separate form.
blocks.directed: You cease attending to the bracelet as a separate form.

blocks.text: You recognise the underlying material reality.
blocks.directed: You recognise the underlying material reality.

blocks.text: Then you consider that the same reality can appear through many different ornaments.
blocks.directed: Then you consider that the same reality can appear through many different ornaments.

blocks.text: The distinction between the forms remains intelligible.
blocks.directed: The distinction between the forms remains intelligible.

blocks.text: But their substantial unity becomes apparent.
blocks.directed: But their substantial unity becomes apparent.

blocks.text: This is only an analogy.
blocks.directed: This is only an analogy.

blocks.text: The tattva system is far more elaborate, and Śiva is not merely an inert substance underlying objects.
blocks.directed: The tattva system is far more elaborate, and Śiva is not merely an inert substance underlying objects.

blocks.text: But it illustrates the direction of contemplation.
blocks.directed: But it illustrates the direction of contemplation.

blocks.text: From differentiation towards source.
blocks.directed: From differentiation towards source.

blocks.text: From appearance towards its ground.
blocks.directed: From appearance towards its ground.

blocks.text: From limited identity towards consciousness.
blocks.directed: From limited identity towards consciousness.

blocks.text: And now Kṣemarāja brings in a rather dramatic method.
blocks.directed: And now Kṣemarāja brings in a rather dramatic method.

blocks.text: The body consumed by fire.
blocks.directed: The body consumed by fire.

blocks.text: He cites the Vijñānabhairava, which describes contemplating a fire arising from the right foot and burning the body, culminating in the appearance of peaceful divine luminosity.
blocks.directed: He cites the Vijñānabhairava, which describes contemplating a fire arising from the right foot and burning the body, culminating in the appearance of peaceful divine luminosity.

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.directed: [short pause] Yes.

blocks.text: A tantric visualisation of your entire body being incinerated.
blocks.directed: A tantric visualisation of your entire body being incinerated.

blocks.text: Lovely.
blocks.directed: [short pause] Lovely.

blocks.text: Very relaxing.
blocks.directed: Very relaxing.

blocks.text: But the fire is imagined within contemplation, not physically applied.
blocks.directed: But the fire is imagined within contemplation, not physically applied.

blocks.text: Nobody needs to set themselves on fire.
blocks.directed: Nobody needs to set themselves on fire.

blocks.text: Nobody needs to damage the body.
blocks.directed: Nobody needs to damage the body.

blocks.text: The aim is to dissolve the mental fixation upon the body as the ultimate identity.
blocks.directed: The aim is to dissolve the mental fixation upon the body as the ultimate identity.

blocks.text: And this is where the philosophical and practical dimensions meet.
blocks.directed: And this is where the philosophical and practical dimensions meet.

blocks.text: Ordinarily you perceive:
blocks.directed: [short pause] Ordinarily you perceive:

blocks.text: “I am this organism, situated in this particular place, surrounded by a separate universe.”
blocks.directed: [short pause] “I am this organism, situated in this particular place, surrounded by a separate universe.”

blocks.text: But through the contemplative dissolution of the embodied principles, that identification is progressively loosened.
blocks.directed: But through the contemplative dissolution of the embodied principles, that identification is progressively loosened.

blocks.text: The body, subtle faculties and differentiated categories are considered in relation to their source.
blocks.directed: The body, subtle faculties and differentiated categories are considered in relation to their source.

blocks.text: Ultimately, that source is consciousness.
blocks.directed: Ultimately, that source is consciousness.

blocks.text: Kṣemarāja connects this practice to dhyāna, meditation, and cites the Mālinīvijayatantra on the methods characteristic of Āṇavopāya, including recitation, meditation, phonemic contemplation and visualisation. Sanskrit & Trika Shaivism.
blocks.directed: Kṣemarāja connects this practice to dhyāna, meditation, and cites the Mālinīvijayatantra on the methods characteristic of Āṇavopāya, including recitation, meditation, phonemic contemplation and visualisation. Sanskrit & Trika Shaivism.

blocks.text: The extraordinary point is that you begin with the very structures through which limitation is experienced.
blocks.directed: The extraordinary point is that you begin with the very structures through which limitation is experienced.

blocks.text: The body.
blocks.directed: The body.

blocks.text: The mind.
blocks.directed: The mind.

blocks.text: The elements.
blocks.directed: The elements.

blocks.text: And use them to contemplate what exceeds their limitations.
blocks.directed: And use them to contemplate what exceeds their limitations.

blocks.text: The prison becomes the meditation hall.
blocks.directed: The prison becomes the meditation hall.

blocks.text: And this is when the text starts getting into yogic physiology.
blocks.directed: And this is when the text starts getting into yogic physiology.

blocks.text: Because apparently dissolving the universe wasn’t quite enough.
blocks.directed: Because apparently dissolving the universe wasn’t quite enough.

blocks.text: Now we’ve got to deal with the plumbing.
blocks.directed: Now we’ve got to deal with the plumbing.
